correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the semigroup by residue classes modulo \(2m\) from \(B+C=2m^2\), identifies each residue slice exactly, and reduces the Frobenius maximum to gap pairs in \(H=\langle n,p\rangle\). Two-generator symmetry converts those gap pairs to the exact spacing \(\lambda_H\). For \(s\ge2\) a strict algebraic inequality puts every residue below the central value; for \(s=1\) a complete split according to whether \(d=m-Q\) lies in \(H\) proves the correction is strictly positive. The modular formula for \(\lambda_H\) follows from a minimal-pair argument. All hypotheses needed for positivity, invertibility of \(B\) modulo \(2m\), and membership of \(m,B,C,Q\) in \(H\) are stated. An exact-integer replay checked 4,418 spacing instances and 743 admissible subthreshold Frobenius numbers, with no discrepancy; enumeration is corroborative rather than the proof.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant 2026 source was read through its theorem, coprime/noncoprime split, and residue decomposition. It proves the simple coprime formula only for \(m\ge2Q\); the new claim treats the disjoint adjacent band \(Q<m<2Q\) and proves that the source formula is always strictly low there, with an exact correction controlled by a two-gap spacing in \(\langle n,p\rangle\). Semantic searches found no published finding with the same generators and subthreshold statement. Earlier Pythagorean-semigroup papers located concern three-generator Pythagorean triples and do not imply the four-generator correction. The current collection was also checked for Frobenius, Pythagorean, numerical-semigroup, semigroup, and Apéry aliases; no existing claim addresses this object or parameter band.

value.rationale: The result resolves the natural boundary question left by the source’s asymmetric main theorem. It gives the exact Frobenius number on the entire contiguous coprime band immediately below \(m=2Q\), proves that the published formula fails at every admissible point of that band, identifies the unique dominant residue, and supplies an explicit modular correction. This is a structural boundary theorem for the same motivating family rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a routine numerical recomputation.
